name: Maneuver Planning Plugin
description: Classical orbital maneuver and ROE targeting operations exposed through a canonical SDK command bridge.

sequentialJustification.detail: Every operation this module exposes is a closed form, a scalar root-find over a handful of doubles, or a bounded integer scan over one of those: a Hohmann transfer is four sqrt() calls, the most expensive root-find (the universal-variable Lambert solve) converges in single-digit iterations, and the only loop whose trip count a caller influences is phasingFromTargetState's revolution-count recommendation, which evaluates one closed form per revolution and whose ceiling is CLAMPED into [1, 100000] rather than trusted — a hostile maxRevs is a typo, not a workload. There is nothing here to shard — the work per invoke is microseconds, and spawning a thread would cost more than the answer. Parallelism over maneuvers belongs to the CALLER, which plans many independent burns; this module holds no cross-call state (its only static is the per-invoke fault latch, cleared at entry), so any number of instances may be driven concurrently by a host that wants throughput. Both thread models compile through the same clang wasm32-wasip1-threads toolchain; this one links no thread-spawn contract because it genuinely never spawns.

methods.description: Executes one named maneuver operation. The port carries a JSON command envelope, not a FlatBuffer: {"operation": "<name>", "params": { ... }} in, a JSON object out. Every failure is a structured error result with an errorCode; no input traps the module.

wildcardJustification.detail: This port does not carry a FlatBuffer and never has. The bridge is JSON-over-bytes: a UTF-8 {"operation": string, "params": object} envelope whose param set is per-operation and is enumerated in analysis/maneuver/README.md. Declaring a concrete SDS identity here would be a fiction of a different shape from the wildcard — the storefront would advertise a schema the bytes do not have, and a consumer that trusted it would decode garbage. There is no ratified SDS record for a maneuver COMMAND envelope today; $MVW (maneuver work order) is the identity this port should carry once minted, and it moves in the same rebuild that adopts it.

acceptedTypeSets.description: UTF-8 JSON command envelope. Not a FlatBuffer; see wildcardJustification.

wildcardJustification.detail: The response is a UTF-8 JSON object whose keys depend on the operation invoked — delta-v scalars, signed RIC component arrays, transfer geometry, solver convergence evidence, and for a refused request an {error, errorCode} pair. Same reasoning as the request port: the bytes are JSON, so no FlatBuffer identity describes them, and $MVW is the pending standard identity for the answer side as well.

acceptedTypeSets.description: UTF-8 JSON result object. Not a FlatBuffer; see wildcardJustification.
